sanskrit: satyasya vacanaṃ śreyaḥ satyajñānaṃ tu duṣkaram yad bhūtahitam atyantam etat satyaṃ bravīmy aham
english: To speak the truth is good, yet the knowledge of truth is hard to win. That which is of utmost benefit to living beings — that I declare to be the truth.

sanskrit: ahaṃkārasya ca tyāgaḥ praṇayasya ca nigrahaḥ saṃtoṣaś caikacaryā ca kūṭasthaṃ śreya ucyate
english: The abandonment of egoism, the restraint of fond craving, contentment, and a solitary course of life — this is called the unshakable, supreme good.

sanskrit: dharmeṇa vedādhyayanaṃ vedāṅgānāṃ tathaiva ca vidyārthānāṃ ca jijñāsā śreya etad asaṃśayam
english: The study of the Vedas according to dharma, and likewise of the Vedāṅgas, and the eager inquiry into the objects of knowledge — this, beyond doubt, is the good.

sanskrit: śabdarūparasasparśān saha gandhena kevalān nātyartham upaseveta śreyaso 'rthī paraṃtapa
english: Sound, form, taste, and touch, together with smell, in their bare forms — let the seeker of the good not pursue these to excess, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: naktaṃcaryā divāsvapnam ālasyaṃ paiśunaṃ madam atiyogam ayogaṃ ca śreyaso 'rthī parityajet
english: Roaming by night, sleeping by day, sloth, slander, intoxicating pride, overexertion and want of effort alike — let the seeker of the good forsake them all.

sanskrit: karmotkarṣaṃ na mārgeta pareṣāṃ parinindayā svaguṇair eva mārgeta viprakarṣaṃ pṛthagjanāt
english: Let him not seek the exaltation of his deeds by disparaging others; by his own virtues alone let him seek to rise above the common run of men.

sanskrit: nirguṇās tv eva bhūyiṣṭham ātmasaṃbhāvino narāḥ doṣair anyān guṇavataḥ kṣipanty ātmaguṇakṣayāt
english: For the most part it is men devoid of merit who think highly of themselves; they assail the virtuous with imagined faults, and so squander what merit they have.

sanskrit: anucyamānāś ca punas te manyante mahājanāt guṇavattaram ātmānaṃ svena mānena darpitāḥ
english: And though no one praises them, they fancy themselves more endowed with virtue than the great, puffed up with their own conceit.

sanskrit: abruvan kasya cin nindām ātmapūjām avarṇayan vipaścid guṇasaṃpannaḥ prāpnoty eva mahad yaśaḥ
english: Uttering no censure of anyone, sounding no praise of himself, the wise man rich in virtue attains, even so, a great renown.

sanskrit: abruvan vāti surabhir gandhaḥ sumanasāṃ śuciḥ tathaivāvyāharan bhāti vimalo bhānur ambare
english: Without a word the fragrant, pure scent of blossoms wafts abroad; and just so, uttering nothing, the spotless sun shines in the sky.

sanskrit: evamādīni cānyāni parityaktāni medhayā jvalanti yaśasā loke yāni na vyāharanti ca
english: These things and others like them, embraced through wisdom, blaze with glory in the world — and yet they make no proclamation of themselves.

sanskrit: na loke dīpyate mūrkhaḥ kevalātmapraśaṃsayā api cāpihitaḥ śvabhre kṛtavidyaḥ prakāśate
english: A fool does not shine in the world by mere self-praise, while the learned man shines forth even though hidden in a pit.

sanskrit: asann uccair api proktaḥ śabdaḥ samupaśāmyati dīpyate tv eva lokeṣu śanair api subhāṣitam
english: A worthless utterance, though loudly proclaimed, soon dies away; but a word well spoken, even softly, shines among the worlds.

sanskrit: mūḍhānām avaliptānām asāraṃ bhāṣitaṃ bahu darśayaty antarātmānaṃ divā rūpam ivāṃśumān
english: The much, pithless talk of the deluded and the arrogant lays bare their inner self, as the radiant sun reveals form by day.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇāt prajñāṃ mṛgayante pṛthagvidhām prajñālābho hi bhūtānām uttamaḥ pratibhāti mām
english: For this reason men seek wisdom of every kind; for the winning of wisdom appears to me the highest gain of living beings.

sanskrit: nāpṛṣṭaḥ kasya cid brūyān na cānyāyena pṛcchataḥ jñānavān api medhāvī jaḍaval lokam ācaret
english: Let him speak to no one unasked, nor to one who questions wrongly; though full of knowledge and keen of mind, let him move through the world as if dull-witted.

sanskrit: tato vāsaṃ parīkṣeta dharmanityeṣu sādhuṣu manuṣyeṣu vadānyeṣu svadharmanirateṣu ca
english: Then let him test his dwelling-place, choosing among good men ever devoted to dharma, among the generous, and among those intent upon their own duty.

sanskrit: caturṇāṃ yatra varṇānāṃ dharmavyatikaro bhavet na tatra vāsaṃ kurvīta śreyorthī vai kathaṃ cana
english: Where the duties of the four varṇas are confounded and overthrown, there let the seeker of the good never make his dwelling, by any means whatever.

sanskrit: nirārambho 'py ayam iha yathālabdhopajīvanaḥ puṇyaṃ puṇyeṣu vimalaṃ pāpaṃ pāpeṣu cāpnuyāt
english: Even one who undertakes no works here, living on whatever comes to hand, gains spotless merit among the meritorious and sin among the sinful.

sanskrit: apām agnes tathendoś ca sparśaṃ vedayate yathā tathā paśyāmahe sparśam ubhayoḥ pāpapuṇyayoḥ
english: As one feels the touch of water, of fire, and of the moon, so do we perceive the touch of both alike — of sin and of merit.

sanskrit: apaśyanto 'nnaviṣayaṃ bhuñjate vighasāśinaḥ bhuñjānaṃ cānnaviṣayān viṣayaṃ viddhi karmaṇām
english: Those who eat the leavings of a sacrifice partake of food without regard to its source; but know that the eating of food's objects is itself the field of works and their fruit.

sanskrit: yatrāgamayamānānām asatkāreṇa pṛcchatām prabrūyād brahmaṇo dharmaṃ tyajet taṃ deśam ātmavān
english: Where, to those who come seeking and inquiring, one would expound the dharma of Brahman with disrespect, that land let the self-possessed man forsake.

sanskrit: śiṣyopādhyāyikā vṛttir yatra syāt susamāhitā yathāvac chāstrasaṃpannā kas taṃ deśaṃ parityajet
english: Where the bond of pupil and teacher is well-ordered and rightly furnished with the scriptures — what man would abandon such a land?

sanskrit: ākāśasthā dhruvaṃ yatra doṣaṃ brūyur vipaścitām ātmapūjābhikāmā vai ko vaset tatra paṇḍitaḥ
english: Where men set on high, hungry for their own honour, would surely fasten fault upon the wise — what learned man would dwell there?

sanskrit: yatra saṃloḍitā lubdhaiḥ prāyaśo dharmasetavaḥ pradīptam iva śailāntaṃ kas taṃ deśaṃ na saṃtyajet
english: Where the dikes of dharma are for the most part churned up and breached by the greedy — who would not forsake that land, as one flees a blazing mountainside?

sanskrit: yatra dharmam anāśaṅkāś careyur vītamatsarāḥ caret tatra vasec caiva puṇyaśīleṣu sādhuṣu
english: Where men, free of misgiving and free of envy, would practise dharma — there let him move and there let him dwell, among the good and righteous of conduct.

sanskrit: dharmam arthanimittaṃ tu careyur yatra mānavāḥ na tān anuvasej jātu te hi pāpakṛto janāḥ
english: But where men would practise dharma only for the sake of gain, let him never dwell among them, for those are people who do evil.

sanskrit: karmaṇā yatra pāpena vartante jīvitespavaḥ vyavadhāvet tatas tūrṇaṃ sasarpāc charaṇād iva
english: Where men cling to life by deeds of sin, from there let him swiftly run away, as from a shelter that holds a serpent.

sanskrit: yena khaṭvāṃ samārūḍhaḥ karmaṇānuśayī bhavet āditas tan na kartavyam icchatā bhavam ātmanaḥ
english: That deed which, having mounted his deathbed, would leave a man clinging in remorse — such a deed he must not do at the outset, if he desires the welfare of his soul.

sanskrit: yatra rājā ca rājñaś ca puruṣāḥ pratyanantarāḥ kuṭumbinām agrabhujas tyajet tad rāṣṭram ātmavān
english: Where the king and the king's men, his close attendants, eat before the householders and seize the first share, that realm let the self-possessed man abandon.

sanskrit: śrotriyās tv agrabhoktāro dharmanityāḥ sanātanāḥ yājanādhyāpane yuktā yatra tad rāṣṭram āvaset
english: But where it is the Vedic scholars, ever devoted to the eternal dharma and engaged in performing sacrifice and teaching, who eat the first share — in such a realm let him take up his abode.

sanskrit: svāhāsvadhāvaṣaṭkārā yatra samyag anuṣṭhitāḥ ajasraṃ caiva vartante vaset tatrāvicārayan
english: Where the cries of Svāhā, Svadhā, and Vaṣaṭ are rightly performed and ceaselessly maintained, there let him dwell without hesitation.

sanskrit: aśucīny atra paśyeta brāhmaṇān vṛttikarśitān tyajet tad rāṣṭram āsannam upasṛṣṭam ivāmiṣam
english: Where he sees impure practices and brāhmaṇas wasted for want of livelihood, that realm let him abandon, as one shuns meat already gone foul.

sanskrit: prīyamāṇā narā yatra prayaccheyur ayācitāḥ svasthacitto vaset tatra kṛtakṛtya ivātmavān
english: Where men in gladness would give even unasked, there let the self-possessed man dwell with tranquil mind, as one whose every task is fulfilled.

sanskrit: daṇḍo yatrāvinīteṣu satkāraś ca kṛtātmasu caret tatra vasec caiva puṇyaśīleṣu sādhuṣu
english: Where punishment falls upon the undisciplined and honour is paid to the self-mastered — there let him move and there let him dwell, among the good of holy conduct.

sanskrit: upasṛṣṭeṣv adānteṣu durācāreṣv asādhuṣu avinīteṣu lubdheṣu sumahad daṇḍadhāraṇam
english: Upon the corrupt and unrestrained, the ill-conducted and the wicked, the undisciplined and the greedy, the wielding of a very great rod of punishment is fitting.

sanskrit: yatra rājā dharmanityo rājyaṃ vai paryupāsitā apāsya kāmān kāmeśo vaset tatrāvicārayan
english: Where a king ever steadfast in dharma rules the realm with care, and the lord of pleasures has cast his desires aside — there let him dwell without hesitation.

sanskrit: tathāśīlā hi rājānaḥ sarvān viṣayavāsinaḥ śreyasā yojayanty āśu śreyasi pratyupasthite
english: For kings of such character swiftly join all the dwellers of their domain to the good, when the good is set before them.

sanskrit: pṛcchatas te mayā tāta śreya etad udāhṛtam na hi śakyaṃ pradhānena śreyaḥ saṃkhyātum ātmanaḥ
english: To you who asked, my child, this account of the good has been declared by me; yet the good of one's own soul cannot be reckoned through any single chief means.

sanskrit: evaṃ pravartamānasya vṛttiṃ praṇihitātmanaḥ tapasaiveha bahulaṃ śreyo vyaktaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: For one who conducts his life thus, with self intent and composed, the good in abundance will plainly come to be, even here, through austerity alone.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca kathaṃ nu muktaḥ pṛthivīṃ cared asmadvidho nṛpaḥ nityaṃ kaiś ca guṇair yuktaḥ saṅgapāśād vimucyate
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: How then may a king such as I, set free, wander the earth, and endowed with what virtues is one ever released from the snare of attachment?

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca atra te vartayiṣyāmi itihāsaṃ purātanam ariṣṭaneminā proktaṃ sagarāyānupṛcchate
english: Bhīṣma said: On this I shall relate to you an ancient tale, spoken by Ariṣṭanemi to Sagara when he questioned him.

sanskrit: sagara uvāca kiṃ śreyaḥ paramaṃ brahman kṛtveha sukham aśnute kathaṃ na śocen na kṣubhyed etad icchāmi veditum
english: Sagara said: What, O holy one, is the highest good, doing which a man enjoys happiness here? How may one neither grieve nor be shaken? This I wish to know.

sanskrit: bhīṣma uvāca evam uktas tadā tārkṣyaḥ sarvaśāstraviśāradaḥ vibudhya saṃpadaṃ cāgryāṃ sad vākyam idam abravīt
english: Bhīṣma said: Thus addressed, Tārkṣya, deeply versed in all the scriptures, perceiving the questioner's surpassing fitness, then spoke this true word.

sanskrit: sukhaṃ mokṣasukhaṃ loke na ca loko 'vagacchati prasaktaḥ putrapaśuṣu dhanadhānyasamākulaḥ
english: The happiness of liberation is happiness indeed in this world, yet the world does not comprehend it — clinging to sons and cattle, distracted with wealth and grain.

sanskrit: saktabuddhir aśāntātmā na sa śakyaś cikitsitum snehapāśasito mūḍho na sa mokṣāya kalpate
english: The man whose mind is bound and whose self is unquiet cannot be healed; deluded, fettered by the noose of fondness, he is not fit for liberation.

sanskrit: snehajān iha te pāśān vakṣyāmi śṛṇu tān mama sakarṇakena śirasā śakyāś chettuṃ vijānatā
english: The bonds born of affection I shall now declare to you — hear them from me; with a head whose ears are open, the discerning man can cut them through.

sanskrit: saṃbhāvya putrān kālena yauvanasthān niveśya ca samarthāñ jīvane jñātvā muktaś cara yathāsukham
english: When in due time you have raised your sons, established them in youth, and known them fit to make their own way in life — then, set free, wander as you please.

sanskrit: bhāryāṃ putravatīṃ vṛddhāṃ lālitāṃ putravatsalām jñātvā prajahi kāle tvaṃ parārtham anudṛśya ca
english: Your wife, grown old, blessed with sons and cherished, fond of her children — knowing her so, forsake her in due season, looking to the higher aim.

sanskrit: sāpatyo nirapatyo vā muktaś cara yathāsukham indriyair indriyārthāṃs tvam anubhūya yathāvidhi
english: With offspring or without, set free, wander as you please, having tasted with your senses the objects of sense in due measure.

sanskrit: kṛtakautūhalas teṣu muktaś cara yathāsukham upapattyopalabdheṣu lābheṣu ca samo bhava
english: Your curiosity for them once satisfied, set free, wander as you please; and toward such gains as come to you by chance, remain even-minded.

sanskrit: eṣa tāvat samāsena tava saṃkīrtito mayā mokṣārtho vistareṇāpi bhūyo vakṣyāmi tac chṛṇu
english: Thus far the matter of liberation has been declared to you by me in brief; I shall now expound it once more at length — hear it.

sanskrit: muktā vītabhayā loke caranti sukhino narāḥ saktabhāvā vinaśyanti narās tatra na saṃśayaḥ
english: The liberated, free of fear, wander happy in the world; but men of clinging nature perish — of this there is no doubt.

sanskrit: āhārasaṃcayāś caiva tathā kīṭapipīlikāḥ asaktāḥ sukhino loke saktāś caiva vināśinaḥ
english: Even insects and ants that hoard their food show this: the unattached are happy in the world, while the attached go to ruin.

sanskrit: svajane na ca te cintā kartavyā mokṣabuddhinā ime mayā vinābhūtā bhaviṣyanti kathaṃ tv iti
english: Nor should you, your mind set on liberation, brood over your kin, thinking, 'How will these fare once parted from me?'

sanskrit: svayam utpadyate jantuḥ svayam eva vivardhate sukhaduḥkhe tathā mṛtyuṃ svayam evādhigacchati
english: A creature is born of itself and of itself grows up; pleasure and pain, and death as well, it meets of its own accord.

sanskrit: bhojanācchādane caiva mātrā pitrā ca saṃgraham svakṛtenādhigacchanti loke nāsty akṛtaṃ purā
english: Their food and clothing, and what is gathered for them by mother and father, men obtain by their own past deeds; nothing in the world comes uncaused by what was done before.

sanskrit: dhātrā vihitabhakṣyāṇi sarvabhūtāni medinīm loke viparidhāvanti rakṣitāni svakarmabhiḥ
english: With their sustenance ordained by the Creator, all living beings run to and fro across the earth, guarded by their own deeds.

sanskrit: svayaṃ mṛtpiṇḍabhūtasya paratantrasya sarvadā ko hetuḥ svajanaṃ poṣṭuṃ rakṣituṃ vādṛḍhātmanaḥ
english: For one who is himself but a lump of clay, forever dependent and infirm of self, what ground is there to nourish his kin or to protect them?

sanskrit: svajanaṃ hi yadā mṛtyur hanty eva tava paśyataḥ kṛte 'pi yatne mahati tatra boddhavyam ātmanā
english: When death strikes down your kin before your very eyes, despite all your great striving — there a man must awaken to the truth within himself.

sanskrit: jīvantam api caivainaṃ bharaṇe rakṣaṇe tathā asamāpte parityajya paścād api mariṣyasi
english: And though this kinsman still lives, you yourself, the task of his support and protection left unfinished, abandoning him, will die hereafter all the same.

sanskrit: yadā mṛtaś ca svajanaṃ na jñāsyasi kathaṃ cana sukhitaṃ duḥkhitaṃ vāpi nanu boddhavyam ātmanā
english: And when you are dead, you will in no way know your kin, whether they are happy or in sorrow — surely a man should awaken to this within himself.

sanskrit: mṛte vā tvayi jīve vā yadi bhokṣyati vai janaḥ svakṛtaṃ nanu buddhvaivaṃ kartavyaṃ hitam ātmanaḥ
english: Whether you be dead or alive, the people will enjoy only the fruit of their own deeds; having understood this, surely a man should do what is for his own true good.

sanskrit: evaṃ vijānaṃl loke 'smin kaḥ kasyety abhiniścitaḥ mokṣe niveśaya mano bhūyaś cāpy upadhāraya
english: Knowing this, and resolved that in this world none truly belongs to another, fix your mind upon liberation, and consider it yet again.

sanskrit: kṣutpipāsādayo bhāvā jitā yasyeha dehinaḥ krodho lobhas tathā mohaḥ sattvavān mukta eva saḥ
english: The embodied one who has here conquered the states of hunger, thirst, and the rest, and anger, greed, and delusion as well — that man of inner strength is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: dyūte pāne tathā strīṣu mṛgayāyāṃ ca yo naraḥ na pramādyati saṃmohāt satataṃ mukta eva saḥ
english: The man who, in gambling, in drink, in women, and in the chase, never grows heedless through infatuation — he is ever liberated indeed.

sanskrit: divase divase nāma rātrau rātrau sadā sadā bhoktavyam iti yaḥ khinno doṣabuddhiḥ sa ucyate
english: He who is wearied by the thought, 'Day after day, night after night, forever and again, one must eat' — that man, they say, is of corrupted understanding.

sanskrit: ātmabhāvaṃ tathā strīṣu muktam eva punaḥ punaḥ yaḥ paśyati sadā yukto yathāvan mukta eva saḥ
english: He who, ever steadfast and rightly discerning, sees the nature of the self in women too as already free, again and again — that man is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: saṃbhavaṃ ca vināśaṃ ca bhūtānāṃ ceṣṭitaṃ tathā yas tattvato vijānāti loke 'smin mukta eva saḥ
english: He who knows in their true reality the arising and the passing away of beings, and their strivings as well — that man in this world is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: prasthaṃ vāhasahasreṣu yātrārthaṃ caiva koṭiṣu prāsāde mañcakasthānaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa mucyate
english: He who sees that, amid thousands of draught-beasts, but a single measure suffices for sustenance, and amid crores of wealth, but the space of a cot within a palace — that man is set free.

sanskrit: mṛtyunābhyāhataṃ lokaṃ vyādhibhiś copapīḍitam avṛttikarśitaṃ caiva yaḥ paśyati sa mucyate
english: He who sees the world smitten by death, oppressed by diseases, and wasted for want of livelihood — that man is set free.

sanskrit: yaḥ paśyati sukhī tuṣṭo napaśyaṃś ca vihanyate yaś cāpy alpena saṃtuṣṭo loke 'smin mukta eva saḥ
english: He who sees thus is happy and content, while he who does not see is undone; and he who is content with little — that man in this world is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: agnīṣomāv idaṃ sarvam iti yaś cānupaśyati na ca saṃspṛśyate bhāvair adbhutair mukta eva saḥ
english: He who beholds that all this is but Agni and Soma, and is not touched by wondrous appearances — that man is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: paryaṅkaśayyā bhūmiś ca samāne yasya dehinaḥ śālayaś ca kadannaṃ ca yasya syān mukta eva saḥ
english: The embodied one to whom a couch for a bed and the bare ground are the same, and fine rice and coarse fare alike — that man is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: kṣaumaṃ ca kuśacīraṃ ca kauśeyaṃ valkalāni ca āvikaṃ carma ca samaṃ yasya syān mukta eva saḥ
english: He to whom linen and a garment of kuśa grass, silk and bark-cloth, wool and hide are all the same — that man is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: pañcabhūtasamudbhūtaṃ lokaṃ yaś cānupaśyati tathā ca vartate dṛṣṭvā loke 'smin mukta eva saḥ
english: He who beholds the world as risen from the five elements, and having so seen it conducts himself accordingly — that man in this world is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: sukhaduḥkhe same yasya lābhālābhau jayājayau icchādveṣau bhayodvegau sarvathā mukta eva saḥ
english: He to whom pleasure and pain are the same, gain and loss, victory and defeat, desire and aversion, fear and agitation — that man in every way is liberated indeed.

sanskrit: raktamūtrapurīṣāṇāṃ doṣāṇāṃ saṃcayaṃ tathā śarīraṃ doṣabahulaṃ dṛṣṭvā cedaṃ vimucyate
english: Seeing this body to be a heap of blood, urine, and dung, a heap of morbid humours rife with corruption — by this very seeing he is set free.

sanskrit: valīpalitasaṃyogaṃ kārśyaṃ vaivarṇyam eva ca kubjabhāvaṃ ca jarayā yaḥ paśyati sa mucyate
english: He who beholds the coming of wrinkles and grey hair, the wasting and the fading of colour, and the bending of the body brought on by old age — that man is set free.

sanskrit: puṃstvopaghātaṃ kālena darśanoparamaṃ tathā bādhiryaṃ prāṇamandatvaṃ yaḥ paśyati sa mucyate
english: He who beholds the failing of his manhood with time, the fading of sight, deafness, and the dulling of the vital breath — that man is set free.
